what: A map-like image, rotated at an angle (299°) and pulled in large (4.5×), is tied to scroll through the section. It straightens with no curve and recedes to 1×, and the offset it sat at (horizontal 66%, vertical .5%) also returns to place. Since the rotation pivot is a point on the image (35% 45%), the ground seems to unfold around that point. It follows slightly late with scrub .3.

options.x: Initial horizontal offset (% of image width), default 66 — brand combines left 50% + 16% against the image width. 0 on phones
options.y: Initial vertical offset (% of image height), default .5 — Brand phone value 29.5
options.origin: Rotation pivot (transform-origin), default 35% 45% — also settable via --fx-origin. Brand phone 42.3% 67.3%
options.end: ScrollTrigger end, default bottom top — until the section has fully left the top of the screen
options.[data-fx-part=stage]: (optional) panel that sticks to the screen while passing through the section — fx.css applies sticky·100vh
options.[data-fx-part=zoom]: Image that is pulled in and pushed back — if absent, the stage’s first child (or the element’s first child)
options.[data-fx-part=turn]: (If present) Layer that spins separately inside zoom — if absent, it spins together with zoom

note: The image starts pulled out larger than its frame, so the frame needs overflow: hidden (the stage sets it by default). To use it as a map where you tap a region after it ends, just paste the map into the section after this part.

from.where: index.js .about .map .translate/.rotate — the pinned regional map rotates 299.12° while shrinking from 4.5x to 1x and then stands upright (original scrub .3 · ease none · target_head one screen)
from.options: Default (desktop) · phone scale: 4.2; x: 0; y: 29.5; origin: 42.3% 67.3%
